title: Design the transform overlay and a simpler way to animate, as mocks
goal: Before building, draw how the person sees and types transform values in a small overlay next to the object (instead of a 3D section in the panel), how the same overlay edits a key's value, how the value graph is edited with points and segments, and how a layer's track shows only what is animated, with a way to add and remove animated properties. The user described the behaviour in detail; the mocks make it concrete and check it against the IA rules.
notes:
User's words (2026-10-12): "I don't really see the point of adding a 3d pane just to show the rotation values. I think when we move or change transitions, we can show a small toolbar like overlay which shows the transform values for typing things in. But doing some other operation or changing the tool makes the transform overlay disappear. On the overlay there should be a reset button to reset to defaults. Also similarly, for when I have a keyframe and click the opacity dot, I want the same overlay to appear to tweak the opacity. Also editing the graph of a particular item like scale is really hard. I can right click on the scale, say show graph, but then when the graph is there, how do I add points on it? I click on the line, doesn't add a point, i can select a point but then if I have 2 points, I can't select the line in between. I want to be able to easily create nice transitions by adding points, selecting the segments between them, right clicking and changing their easing, etc. I need the ia to be consistent across the properties. When I add a 'key' to a video, it adds all of the animatable properties below it. I really wish there was a more scalable solution to the ux here, because we really should only show the properties being animated. And, if we want to clear one of them, i should be able to select one of the rows and hit delete to remove the whole property from being animated. but there should be a way to add it back. like maybe the keyframe line should be selectable and right clicked to animate a variety of things. or I can click it, tweak something (like transform) and the options are automatically added to that keyframe."

Five tasks, in order: the design (mocks), then the transform overlay, the key value overlay, the graph editor, and only-animated-properties with auto-key. Code pointers (read, not run): the 3D section is Space3DInspector (Sources/Photonz/Space3DInspector.swift, shown at InspectorPanel.swift:1526) with EditorState+Space3D.swift; key lanes and the graph toggle are KeyLanesView.swift (segments at :270, lane menus :156, :213, :423) and EditorState+KeyLanes.swift (:283 'Show Graph'); Add Key on a clip is EditorState+TimelineMenus.swift:199 and per property EditorState+PropertyKeys.swift:177 addKeyHere; the property strip is MotionStripView.swift. The shared curve list is EasingCurve (PhotonzCore/LayerMotion.swift) with Draw a Curve, and CurveRow from every-transition-can-be-picked-from-presets-and. Memory rules: one purpose per area (the IA contract in docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md decides placement), mocks are the floor, legible text, no em dashes in UI copy. This is step 1 of 5.
acceptance: Mock pages under docs/design/mocks/pages/ on the shared shell: (1) the transform overlay: a compact glass bar near the picked object while moving, resizing, rotating or tilting it, with typeable X, Y, W, H, Rotation, Tilt X, Tilt Y, Depth (only the ones that apply), a Reset button, and where it sits so it never covers the handle being dragged; (2) the same overlay opened from a key dot (for example an opacity key) showing that property's value at that key; (3) the graph editor with points, a hovered and a picked segment, the right-click easing menu on a segment, and adding a point by clicking the line; (4) a layer's track showing only animated properties, a picked property row, Delete, the clip key line's right-click Animate menu, and auto-key adding a row when a value changes at a key

The placement of each piece is checked against the IA placement contract (UX-PATTERNS.md) and the contract is updated with the overlay as a named canvas element (transient, appears with a transform, leaves with the next operation or tool change)
One interaction table in the mock for keys and graphs that is the same for every property (position, scale, rotation, opacity, tilt, depth, colour, blur and the rest)
A decision card links the mocks for the user; the four build tasks follow the mocks and only wait on the card for a real fork
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
